alert.name: ConsumerLagHigh
alert.summary: The ledger consumer group is 250 messages behind on the topic provider-events, all partitions together; the threshold is 50.

diagnosis.hypothesis: False alarm. The ledger consumer group is not 250 messages behind. Its lag on provider-events stayed at 0 to 1 from 19:49 through 19:54, when the alert fired. The ledger posts events about as fast as payment-confirmer confirms them. The money check settled in 0.24s and all five invariants passed, so every provider event up to the cutoff was booked exactly once. The stack came up at 19:48:52 and nothing has restarted or changed since. The 250 figure most likely comes from the alert rule: a bad expression or labels (the metric has consumer, partition, service_instance_id, service_name, not consumer_group), a stale series from before bring-up, or an injected test alert. I could not see the rule, so its exact fault stays open. A spike shorter than my 60s samples is possible but would have cleared almost at once, and nothing was lost.

evidence.shows: Ledger consumer lag summed by consumer is 0 to 1 from 19:49 to 19:54:26, never near 250. payment-confirmer is at 0.
Total lag across all consumers is 0 over the window, including right after the 19:54:18 firing time.
The lag metric's labels are consumer, partition, service_instance_id and service_name. There is no consumer_group label, so a rule grouping on it would be wrong.
The ledger consumer is steadily posting events (about 3.5/s posted, plus a few already_processed duplicates handled safely), in line with the confirmer's rate.
The money check passed after settling in 0.24s: all 1134 provider events posted exactly once, ledger balanced, matching the provider, and payments and refunds matching. Nothing is backed up.
All containers are running and healthy with 0 restarts. ledger-consumer started at 19:49:00.
The only deploys are the initial bring-up at 19:48:52. Ledger settings are normal (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter). No later change could cause a backlog.

proposed_fix.summary: Change nothing in the payments system. Check the ConsumerLagHigh rule's expression and labels against klaxon_kafka_consumer_lag, which is labeled by consumer, not consumer_group. Also check whether the rule could have read stale series from before the 19:48 bring-up. Fix the rule if it is wrong, and keep watching ledger lag for a recurrence.

diagnosis.blast_radius: No system change is proposed. Editing the alert rule affects only alerting. A mistake there could hide real ledger lag, so test the new expression against current data before relying on it.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the alert rule is edited, restore its previous definition from version control.
